Evidence synthesis reporting item bank

Reporting items and concepts from 59 evidence synthesis reporting guidelines, searchable and downloadable

Evidence synthesis reporting item bank

2,307 reporting items from 59 evidence synthesis reporting guidelines (83 publications, 68 checklists, 1999 to 2025), each broken down into the 4,584 reporting concepts it asks for. Filter, search and download the data below.

GitHub repository Study registration (OSF) Browse the data How to cite
NoteHow to use this page
  • Guidelines lists each included publication with its type, methodology and discipline. Reporting items holds every item verbatim. Concepts holds the standardised reporting concepts extracted from each item.
  • Drop-down filters above each table combine with AND logic. The boxes under each column heading filter that column; the search box searches all columns.
  • Download filtered exports the rows currently matched by your filters and searches. The links under each table give the full CSV files.
  • The reporting item and concept tables can be joined on checklist_item_id; all three tables can be joined on study_id.

Datasets

Guidelines

Filter the guidelines

One row per publication. A guideline published in several journals (for example PRISMA 2020) has several rows sharing one guideline ID.

Full guideline table (CSV)

Reporting items

Filter the reporting items

Items are reproduced verbatim from each checklist. “Section” is the standardised manuscript section used in the analyses; “Section in guideline” is the heading used by the guideline itself. Five “not applicable” placeholder rows from the PRISMA-ScR checklist are not shown.

Full item bank (CSV) Items by section (Excel)

Concepts

Filter the concepts

One row per concept per item. An item that asks for several things has several rows; the same concept recurs across items and guidelines. Concepts are worded generically so they can be compared across methodologies (“Report the methodology used to conduct the evidence synthesis” rather than “Identify the report as a systematic review”).

Full concept table (CSV) Concepts by section (Excel)

Citation and reuse

If you use these data, please cite the accompanying paper (reference to be added on publication) and the repository:

Morrison K, Ivimey-Cook ER, Lagisz M, Mizuno A, Santana MS, Santos ESA, Sánchez-Tójar A, Simpson ZP, Grainger M, Macura B, Nakagawa S. An item bank of reporting items and concepts in evidence synthesis reporting guidelines. GitHub repository: https://github.com/KyleMorrison99/synthesis_item_bank.

The data and code are released under the licence in the repository. You are welcome to fork or clone the repository, open an issue to suggest corrections or additional guidelines, and build on the item bank for new reporting guidance.
